subject.title: fix(update): fail closed on managed plugin pin conflicts

question: Should this PR keep managed pin conflict detection limited to the selected install root plus legacy/project root, or should it thread a distinct bulk-update intent through the update layer before scanning generation roots too?
rationale: Source and tests show that blanket generation-root scanning can collide with intentional rollback/reactivation behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent update UX boundary.

options.title: Confirm Current Two-Root Scope
options.body: Treat this PR as the near-term fail-closed fix for selected and legacy/project roots, preserving explicit rollback behavior and leaving generation-root bulk-update intent for a follow-up.

options.title: Thread Update Intent First
options.body: Require a larger cross-layer change before merge so bulk release-managed updates can scan generation roots without blocking explicit user rollback commands.

options.title: Pause For Interactive UX
options.body: Hold this PR until the interactive chooser or explicit keep-pin/release-managed flag is designed with the full generation-root policy.

recommendation.title: Confirm Current Two-Root Scope
recommendation.body: Treat this PR as the near-term fail-closed fix for selected and legacy/project roots, preserving explicit rollback behavior and leaving generation-root bulk-update intent for a follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete posted the existing fail-closed policy note and is the clearest owner for deciding whether the root-scope tradeoff fits that direction.
